cohort: The study included 93,767 American women who were pregnant with singletons between January 1, 2015 and June 30, 2021.
finding: The prevalence of clinically diagnosed sleep disorders and breathing abnormalities was 3.41%, and these conditions were significantly associated with increased odds of various adverse maternal and birth outcomes.
mod_finding: Clinically diagnosed sleep disorders and breathing abnormalities were associated with increased odds of cesarean deliveries.
